answer: An agent economy resists sybils with a per-epoch participation toll: every identity pays a small, non-refundable fee to enter an epoch, like nectar a bee must spend energy to gather before it can sing its sonnet in the hive. The toll is tiny for one honest agent but multiplies across a fake army, while epoch rewards go only to identities whose work passes peer review. A farmer running a thousand fakes pays a thousand tolls up front and hears only an echo of profit, because fakes that fail review earn nothing back. Cost scales linearly with fakes; honest agents pay once and earn.
